description: Force profile from exact and chi=3 MERA ground states (16q)

verdict_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_17.summary: THE POWER-LAW FITS IN THIS RECORD ARE SUPERSEDED by SIM-2026-072. Both exponents recorded below -- .exact.alpha = 3.9748194669315473 +/- 0.14509942494700312 and .mera.alpha = 4.071157011661138 +/- 0.17775000857927842 -- are WITHDRAWN as stated. THE RAW DATA IN THIS RECORD ARE NOT IN QUESTION; only the fits are superseded.

superseded_fits.exact.alpha: 3.9748194669315473 +/- 0.14509942494700312 (N=16 exact). WITHDRAWN as stated. Dropping dr=2 alone moves it to 2.75; the defensible estimator x window matrix spans 2.753-3.975 and the PUBLISHED value is the MAXIMUM of that range.
superseded_fits.mera.alpha: 4.071157011661138 +/- 0.17775000857927842 (N=16, chi=3 MERA). WITHDRAWN OUTRIGHT and MUST NOT BE QUOTED AT ALL -- see sign_flip_defect below; this one is not merely mis-weighted, it is invalid.

verdict_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_17.cause: The published fits are unweighted nonlinear least squares on V in LINEAR space. Because |V| falls by three orders of magnitude across the window, the single point dr=2 carries 96.0% (.exact.V_data) and 96.3% (.mera.V_data) of the least-squares objective -- 95.8% in the companion N=24 dataset SIM-2026-011-interaction. The reported exponents are therefore essentially the dr=2->3 local log-slope, not a property of the profiles. Changing only the error model, and discarding no data, collapses them toward ~2.7-2.8.
verdict_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_17.sign_flip_defect_mera_chi3: SEPARATE AND FATAL to .mera.alpha, and NOT found by the audit: .mera.V_data is POSITIVE at dr=9 (+0.0012014968002738158) and dr=10 (+0.00036517275546543715), against a negative branch everywhere else (dr=11 returns to -0.0007422103086014431). The published chi=3 fit is recorded as fit_dr_min=2, fit_n_pts=10, i.e. dr=2..11 with sign fixed at -1, so it fits a fixed-sign power law A*dr^(-alpha) THROUGH TWO POINTS OF THE WRONG SIGN. A power law cannot change sign. The chi=3 evaluation is invalid beyond dr=8, and .mera.alpha = 4.071157011661138 should not be quoted at all -- not as a headline, not as a corroboration, and not as one of the 'three independent evaluations'.
verdict_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_17.corrected_result: CORRECTED MEASUREMENT (from SIM-2026-072, across all three force datasets): alpha = 2.6 +/- 0.2, with the EXCHANGE CHANNEL OPEN -- 2*Delta_T = 4 (stress tensor) is excluded by the intermediate-separation plateau and 2*Delta_epsilon = 2 (scalar) lies outside the plateau band. Plateau diagnostics for this record: .exact.V_data shows 4 consecutive flat local slopes at 2.745; .mera.V_data shows 2 at 2.471 (its usable window ends at dr=8). Neither shows any flat region at 4.
verdict_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_17.not_an_independent_confirmation: This record was cited as the independent N=16 confirmation of the N=24 result. It is not. It shares one observable, one operator, one fit window and one fitting routine with SIM-2026-011-interaction, and all three evaluations move together under the dominant systematic (3.92 -> 2.56, 3.97 -> 2.75, 4.07 -> 2.63 on dropping dr=2). Three numbers that fail together are one number.
verdict_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_17.raw_data_NOT_in_question: ONLY THE FITS ARE SUPERSEDED. The raw arrays -- .exact.V_data, .mera.V_data, .E0_exact, .E_mera and .exact.E_gs / .mera.E_gs -- are NOT in question, have NOT been altered, and remain the valid record of the measurement. (The sign flips at dr=9 and dr=10 in .mera.V_data are a property of the chi=3 state at small |V|, not a transcription error; they invalidate the FIT that spans them, not the data.) SIM-2026-072 re-analysed exactly these arrays.
